Tamil }} '''''Kuberaa''''' is a 2025 Indian [[action drama]] film{{cite web|url=https://www.bbfc.co.uk/release/kuberaa-q29sbgvjdglvbjpwwc0xmdmwnjex|title=Kuberaa|website=[[British Board of Film Classification]]|quote=A group of beggars become embroiled in a corrupt businessman's unscrupulous scheme in this action drama.}} directed by [[Sekhar Kammula]], who co-wrote the screenplay with Chaithanya Pingali. Produced by Sree Venkateswara Cinemas LLP and [[Amigos Creations]], the film was simultaneously shot in [[Telugu language|Telugu]] and [[Tamil language|Tamil]]. It stars [[Dhanush]], [[Nagarjuna (actor)|Nagarjuna]], [[Rashmika Mandanna]] and [[Jim Sarbh]].{{Cite web |date=18 June 2025 |title=Sekhar Kammula on 'Kuberaa' and his next plans |url=https://telugucinema.com/news/sekhar-kammula-on-kuberaa-and-his-next-plans |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250619122724/https://telugucinema.com/news/sekhar-kammula-on-kuberaa-and-his-next-plans |archive-date=19 June 2025 |access-date=19 June 2025 |website=[[Telugucinema.com]]}} The film was announced in June 2021. [[Principal photography]] took place between February 2024 and April 2025. The film has music composed by [[Devi Sri Prasad]], cinematography by [[Niketh Bommireddy]], editing by [[Karthika Srinivas]] and production design by [[Thota Tharani]]. ''Kuberaa'' was released worldwide on 20 June 2025 to highly positive reviews from critics, with praise for its concept and Dhanush's performance while criticisms were highlighted at its runtime and climax. The film was a box office success in [[Telugu language|Telugu]] but a [[box office failure]] in [[Tamil language|Tamil]], grossing {{Indian rupee|115–132 crore}}.{{efn|name="bo"|''Kuberaa''{{'}}s |url-status=live }} == Plot == Neeraj Mitra, a Mumbai businessman, discovers an oil reserve hidden in the [[Bay of Bengal]]. Eager to turn it into a source of wealth, he plans a mission along with his business tycoon dad, with the backing of Minister Sidappa, and he sends a team to brutally kill the oil reserve workers and explode it. To make it work, he turns to Deepak Tej, an ex-[[Central Bureau of Investigation|C.B.I.]] officer now in prison for refusing to bow to corruption. Left with no choice, Deepak agrees to help. Though he does not share Neeraj's greed, his circumstances force him into the plan. Deepak gathers a group of beggars and makes them [[Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988|benami]]s, creating fake companies in their name and transferring funds between them. The beggars, Khelu, Dibya, Kushboo, and Deva Kallam, from across the country to carry out the job quietly in Mumbai. Deva, a kind-hearted, naive man from [[Tirupati]], along with the other beggars have no idea what they have been dragged into. All four beggars are made to stay at a house with a cruel man named Robo, who takes advantage of the beggars and removes one of Khelu's teeth after he stole Kushboo's money. Deva gains blind trust for Deepak, who reminds him of his now-dead brother Obulesh. Eventually, Robo kills Khelu and Dibya after their financial transactions are complete. Deva calls Deepak and tells him that Khelu is missing. Afterwards, Neeraj talks with Deepak and tells him that he plans to kill the beggars after they are done with them, which Deepak has second thoughts about. Robo takes advantage of pregnant Kushboo, but Deva defends her. Eventually, Deva completes an iris scan, and Robo takes him to a secluded spot to kill him but he escapes. This sparks a manhunt with Neeraj and Deepak racing to find him before the truth unravels, and they face the dire consequences of losing him. On the run, Deva meets Sameera, who has been stranded in Mumbai after her boyfriend jilted her. Deva almost dies after Robo catches him, but some dogs go after Robo and eat half of his arm. Deepak goes to Tirupati in search of him after being instructed to do so by Neeraj. Deva frequents Sameera, who now stays in a women's hostel after her friend's father did not let her stay at their place. They live off of Kushboo's money, as she left a small box of money and told Deva that he should use it if anything happened to her. She helps Deva to meet Narayan Gaikwad, one of the people Deva had a transaction with, who was killed by Neeraj. Deva tells the [[Sub-Inspector|sub-inspector]] Ashok about the transaction, but the lack of details meant that Deva was thrown in jail for a petty case. After recognising Neeraj's photo in a newspaper, Ashok agrees to let Deva help him in his investigation. Deva leads him to a room in a flat building, which Narayan frequents, and the two find suitcases of money and gold bars Deepak hunts down the location of Deva and Ashok and Deepak subsequently kills Ashok. Deva sneaks up behind Deepak, who traced his location, and hits him on the head with a rock. Deepak, who reformed after seeing how inhumane Neeraj is, tells Deva and Sameera that he wants to help them after they keep him captive. Deva tells Deepak about how he wants all of the beggars in various cities to have necessities, and Deepak tells Deva that to expose Neeraj, they need evidence. Deepak reveals to them that Kushboo is still alive and well, and Deva demands that he meet Kushboo. Robo and his team track down their location and catch Kushboo, but Deva attacks him, and Kushboo goes into labour. Deepak protects them by killing Robo and his men, but Kushboo dies after giving birth to her son, and Deepak is shot in the process. Before dying, he asks Deva to think of him as Obulesh, Deva's brother, leaving Deva and Sameera devastated. As Deva and Sameera perform the last rites for Deepak and Kushboo, they discuss their plans, and Deva decides to protect Kushboo's son. Deva helps a lorry driver unload crores of money that was stored in a storage locker in front of Neeraj's house. Neeraj asks Deva what his demands are, and Deva tells Neeraj that he should live as a beggar for one day. Despite living as a beggar for one day, Neeraj does not reform, as he does not take his job seriously and doesn't ask for alms, as he intends to find Deva. A fight in a garbage landfill leads Deva killing Neeraj. Sidappa strikes another deal for his oil rig while Deva brings Kushboo's son to Tirupati, where a beggar names him ''Kuberaa''. == Cast == {{Cast listing| * [[Dhanush]] as Deva Kalam ** Sai Suresh as young Deva * [[Nagarjuna (actor)|Nagarjuna]] as Deepak Tej/Obulesh * [[Rashmika Mandanna]] as Sameera * [[Jim Sarbh]] as Neeraj Mitra * [[Hareesh Peradi]] as R. He filed a complaint, but was not responded to. |url-status=live }} == Reception == === Critical response === Avad Mohammad of ''[[OTTPlay]]'' gave 4/5 stars and wrote "''Kuberaa'' is one of the best Telugu films in recent times. With gripping thrills, heartfelt emotions, a compelling story, and a powerful message, the film delivers on every front."{{Cite web |last=Mohammad |first=Avad |date=20 June 2025 |title=Kuberaa Review: Dhanush mesmerizes in Sekhar Kammula's boldest film yet |url=https://www.ottplay.com/review/kuberaa-review-dhanush-mesmerizes-in-sekhar-kammulas-boldest-film-yet/5666d5970b522 |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=[[OTTPlay]] }} Paul Nicodemus of ''[[The Times of India]]'' gave 3.5/5 stars and wrote "Kuberaa is not your usual commercial potboiler—and that's precisely what makes it worth a watch. It's a brooding, introspective take on wealth and morality. It's not flawless, but it's a bold leap from a filmmaker unafraid to reinvent his canvas."{{Cite web |last=Nicodemus |first=Paul |date=2025-06-21 |title=Kuberaa Movie Review: Dhanush and Nagarjuna anchor a brooding, thought-provoking social drama |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/telugu/movie-reviews/kuberaa/movie-review/121974766.cms |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=[[The Times of India]] }} Swaroop Kodur of ''[[The Indian Express]]'' gave 3.5/5 stars and wrote "''Kuberaa'' wears its bleeding heart on its sleeve for the marginalised, and while several scenes are effective, a few others feel repetitive and yank the pacing.[...] If the bloated duration of the film could be overlooked, Kuberaa stands apart from all the cacophony around as a one-of-a-kind 'mass' experience."{{Cite web |last=Kodur |first=Swaroop |date=2025-06-20 |title=Kuberaa movie review: Dhanush and Nagarjuna shine bright in Sekhar Kammula's mindful 'massy' film |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/movie-review/kuberaa-movie-review-dhanush-shines-bright-in-mindful-massy-film-10078003/ |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=[[The Indian Express]] }} BH Harsh of ''[[Cinema Express]]'' gave 3.5/5 stars and wrote "Dhanush's performance, aided by Sekhar's direction, does wonders here. [...] ''Kuberaa'' is a bold stroke of filmmaking, staunch in its commentary and so affecting in its sentiment. A few quibbles can be ignored."{{Cite web |last=Harsh |first=B. H. |date=2025-06-20 |title=Kuberaa Movie Review: A searingly humane socio-political thriller |url=https://www.cinemaexpress.com/telugu/review/2025/Jun/20/kuberaa-movie-review-a-searingly-humane-socio-political-thriller |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=[[Cinema Express]] }} Janani K of ''[[India Today]]'' gave 3/5 stars and wrote "''Kuberaa'' raises important questions about justice, money and power. But, it is not one without flaws. The pre-climax and climax feel a bit rushed and lack emotional connect. That said, ''Kuberaa'' presents a world that will keep you intrigued."{{Cite web |last=K |first=Janani |date=2025-06-20 |title=Kuberaa review: Compelling premise meets conventional end in Dhanush-Nagarjuna film |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/reviews/story/kuberaa-movie-review-dhanush-nagarjuna-compelling-premise-conventional-ending-sekhar-kammula-2743667-2025-06-20 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250620134109/https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/reviews/story/kuberaa-movie-review-dhanush-nagarjuna-compelling-premise-conventional-ending-sekhar-kammula-2743667-2025-06-20 |archive-date=20 June 2025 |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=[[India Today]] }} Kirubhakar Purushothaman of ''[[News18]]'' gave 3/5 stars and wrote "While Kuberaa carefully steers away from the generic nature of commercial entertainers, the end seems like an easy way out and undermines its desire to be unique."{{Cite web |last=Purushothaman |first=Kirubhakar |date=June 20, 2025 |title=Kuberaa Review: Dhanush, Nagarjuna's Film Is A Predictable But Engaging Tale Of Greed |url=https://www.news18.com/movies/reviews/kuberaa-review-dhanush-nagarjuna-rashmika-mandanna-jim-sarbh-film-is-a-predictable-but-engaging-tale-of-greed-ws-l-9395793.html |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=[[News18]] }} Sangeetha Devi Dundoo of ''[[The Hindu]]'' wrote "Kuberaa falls short of being a gamechanger. But it is a brave film from a director who has often stepped away from the norm, and raised pertinent questions. That is ample reason to cheer."{{Cite news |last=Dundoo |first=Sangeetha Devi |date=2025-06-20 |title='Kuberaa' movie review: Sekhar Kammula's brave film is imperfect, yet compelling |url=https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/movies/kuberaa-movie-review-dhanush-nagarjuna-akkineni-rashmika-mandanna-sekhar-kammula/article69716924.ece |access-date=2025-06-21 |work=[[The Hindu]] }} === Box office === ''Kubera'' grossed ₹13 crore net on its opening day in India,{{cite news |title=Kuberaa box office collection day 1: Dhanush-starrer has a smaller opening than Kamal Haasan's Thug Life, earns Rs 13 crore |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/telugu/kuberaa-box-office-collection-day-1-dhanush-starrer-ears-rs-13-crore-smaller-opening-than-kamal-haasan-thug-life-10079404/ |work=The Indian Express |date=21 June 2025 }} with a worldwide gross of ₹26 crore, marking Dhanush's highest opening day collection.{{Citation needed|date=October 2025}} On its second day, the film earned an estimated ₹17 crore net in India, pushing the global gross past ₹50 crore.{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}} The third day saw collections of ₹18.5 crore net in India, resulting in a domestic weekend total of ₹48.5 crore and a global gross of approximately ₹79 crore.{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}} On the fourth day, earnings dropped to ₹7.25 crore net in India.{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}} By the end of its first week, the film had grossed an estimated ₹104 crore worldwide, with ₹78 crore from India and ₹26 crore from overseas markets.{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}} The Telugu version was commercially successful but the Tamil version significantly underperformed.
